metadata.note: The Mobile, Jackson and Kansas City Railroad (1897-1909) and its predecessors and successor before the Gulf, Mobile and Northern: Mobile - Laurel - Newton - Pontotoc - Middleton with the Hattiesburg and Ellisville branches. Drawn per the research report's drawable: spans. Rule 4 splits: MJ&KC -> New Orleans, Mobile and Chicago at the Dec 1, 1909 takeover (NOM&C features share the MJ&KC geometry); Gulf and Chicago -> MJ&KC at the July 1, 1903 change of control (MJ&KC's 'Gulf and Chicago Division' shares the G&C geometry). The 3-ft Ship Island, Ripley and Kentucky (Middleton - Ripley, 1874-1875) and Kingston and Central Mississippi (Laurel - Bay Springs, 1902 [ANCHOR]) are their own companies with years that touch no other feature's. The MJ&KC main line is one feature per section because each section's first confirmed year differs (1897, 1898, 1899, 1903, 1906, 1907, 1903). Receiverships (MJ&KC 1906-09, NOM&C 1913-16) and the Frisco/L&N stock control of the NOM&C (1911-12) are not operator changes. The GM&N continuation (from 1919 [OPEN]) is in gulf_mobile_and_northern_railroad.geojson. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout (see each segment note and speed_source).
sources: Lemly, James H., The Gulf, Mobile and Ohio (1953), ch. V and XXII, https://acmeme.com/gmo/chapter_xxii.htm
Official Guide pages on Mississippi Rails: G&C Mar 1900; MJ&KC Apr 1900, Jan 1904, July 1907; K&CM July 1902; NOM&C Sept 1910 - https://www.msrailroads.com/Timetables/
Chronicling America: Hattiesburg News 1916-03-10 p.6; Greene County Herald 1914-01-09 p.1
metadata.geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL). The main line (Mobile - Middleton) and every main-line section reuse the GM&N layer's opstrace.py trace (dataset PR #280, features gmn-mobile-union and gmn-union-middleton, over ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror), cut at Nominatim station points projected onto the line, plus a 0.6 mi opstrace.py extension at Mobile to Frascati. The Hattiesburg Branch was traced fresh with opstrace.py over the CN Beaumont Subdivision (OSM old_railway_operator='Bonhomie and Hattiesburg Southern Railroad'); the Ellisville Branch over the old_railway_operator=GM&O 'Spur Line Road' way plus two labelled straight legs. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for both branch areas and returned nothing.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] end: nomc-mobile-middleton 1915 - NOM&C passenger service in 1916 is near-certain (it handed the GM&N an operating railroad Jan 1, 1917) but unproven; a 1916 Guide or 1916 newspaper item would let it run to 1916.
1917-1918 on the through line: undrawn on both this layer and the GM&N layer (GM&N starts 1919 [OPEN]). A known gap, not an assertion of no service.
[OPEN] ends: nomc-hattiesburg-branch and nomc-ellisville-branch 1910 - no passenger evidence after the May 15, 1910 table; 1911-1916 not established either way.
[OPEN] start: gc-middleton-pontotoc 1899 - Gulf and Chicago passenger service 1890-1898 implied by the 1895 roster, unproven by timetable.

[OPEN] end: sirk-middleton-ripley 1875 - SIR&K service 1876-1889 implied by the 1879 roster, no timetable found. Ripley RR opening Aug 30, 1872 (Lemly) vs 1874 (Hoffman); Ripley -> SIR&K rename 1872 (Lemly) vs 1878 (Hoffman). Ripley - Pontotoc (G&SI Northern Division) 1887-1898: no passenger evidence.
[ANCHOR]: kcm-laurel-bay-springs 1902 - did K&CM passenger service begin in 1901, and did the MJ&KC run it July - Dec 1902 before shutting it down?

Brackets not drawn: Lucedale - Merrill 1898 (Lemly 'opened in 1898', no passenger evidence); Merrill - Beaumont and the Hattiesburg Branch Nov 1902 (Lemly) or Feb 1902 (Mississippi Rails) - Dec 1903; Laurel - Newton and the Ellisville Branch 1904-1906 (first timetable March 1907).

Mobile terminal: the NOM&C's new passenger and freight terminal of Dec 1, 1911 is not located (Lemly's 1909 plan: Augusta and Royal Sts); 1911-1915 is drawn to Frascati. The exact Frascati station site is not verified (drawn to today's TASD Frascati Yard).
G&C -> MJ&KC instrument: 'purchased control' (Lemly) vs 'leased' (msrailroads); split year 1903 either way.
NOM&C trains Laurel - New Orleans over the NO&NE, Mar 1, 1912 - June 1, 1913: were any passenger trains? Not drawn.
Greene County Herald Cotton Plant wreck: LoC dates the issue 1914-01-09, masthead OCR reads 1913.

Hattiesburg Branch geometry: OSM tags the surviving line as the Bonhomie and Hattiesburg Southern; identity with the MJ&KC branch rests on Fowler's identical station lists, and the MJ&KC/NOM&C Hattiesburg terminals are not located.
Headways and speeds are estimates (printed schedules only: 1899 Mobile - Merrill, 1899 G&C, 1907 Ellisville, 1910 through line).
omitted: Block [12] NOM&C Laurel - New Orleans over the NO&NE (Mar 1912 - June 1913): no confirmed passenger train - Lemly frames these as a freight bridge.
Block [13] is evidence for the NOM&C through line's end, not a separate feature; it governs nomc-mobile-middleton's 1915 [OPEN] end.
Ripley - Pontotoc before 1899 (Gulf and Ship Island Northern Division, 1887-89, and the G&C before 1899): no passenger evidence (drawable NONE).

Kingston Lumber Co. logging railroad Laurel - Bay Springs c.1899 - Aug 1901; Frascati / Choctaw Point dock tracks; the 1870s Mobile and Northwestern grade (never ran a train): freight or no service (Rule 1).
Proposed extensions never built: Ovett - near New Orleans, Beaumont - Ansley/Pearl River, Middleton - Atwood/Bolivar; Chickasaw spur (built 1925 by the GM&N, freight).

segments.note: Mobile (Frascati) - Dog River (Latonia, just inside Mississippi). Start 1897 is exact to the year: Fowler's line-55 letter z is the October 1897 Official Guide, and 'Dog River z(tm)' marks it as the terminus of service then. Construction began Dec 1896 (Lemly ch. XXII). Aug 21, 1899 table: three trains each way Mobile - Merrill. Receivers operated the same company from Dec 26, 1906 (not an operator change). End 1909 = foreclosure and the New Orleans, Mobile and Chicago takeover on Dec 1, 1909; service continues on feature nomc-mobile-middleton. headway_min 480 = the three trains each way of the 1899 table; an estimate for other years.
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide Apr 1900 (schedule Aug 21, 1899); Fowler MS line 55 (z: 10/1897G; 1898G names); Lemly ch. XXII; Official Guide Jan 1904, July 1907, Sept 1910 (research report block [1]).

Merrill - Beaumont was built by June 1, 1902 and carried the 1902-03 Mobile - Hattiesburg service, but no 1902 passenger evidence was found (SOURCE CONFLICT on the Hattiesburg extension's opening: Nov 17, 1902 per Lemly, Feb 1902 per the Mississippi Rails corporate history), so the 1902-1903 bracket is not drawn. End 1909 = NOM&C takeover Dec 1, 1909. headway_min 480 = three trains each way (1907 table); an estimate.

segments.note: Newton - Decatur Junction - Union - Philadelphia - Louisville - Ackerman - Mathiston - Houston - Pontotoc (the line built 1905-06 to close the gap between the MJ&KC and the Gulf and Chicago). Newton - Decatur opened June 19, 1905; the entire line opened for commercial transportation Apr 16, 1906 (Lemly). Start 1906 rests on Fowler's '1906Glist' (1906 Official Guide station names Hathorn and Livingston on this section); first timetable seen is April 7, 1907 (July 1907 Guide). Pontotoc station closed by injunction Mar 11 - Apr 13, 1906. Built by the Gulf and Chicago Railway under MJ&KC control and operated by the MJ&KC. End 1909 = NOM&C takeover Dec 1, 1909. headway_min 480 = three through trains each way (1907); an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide July 1907 p.1022 ('April 7, 1907'); Sept 1910 p.1001; Fowler MS line 55 ('1906Glist'); Lemly ch. XXII; msrailroads NOM&C photo captions (research report block [5]).

segments.note: Pontotoc - New Albany - Ripley - Falkner - Middleton, run by the MJ&KC as its 'Gulf and Chicago Division' after taking control of the Gulf and Chicago July 1, 1903 (purchase of control per Lemly, lease per msrailroads - moot for drawing). Jan 1904 Guide table dated September 20, 1903: three trains each way, superintendent C. F. Morgan at Ripley. 3-ft gauge until converted: New Albany - Pontotoc reopened standard gauge June 20, 1904, New Albany - Middleton June 27, 1905 (Lemly) - 'reopened' implies short closures whose length is not established. The new Gulf and Chicago Railway corporation (1903-1909) existed on paper; the trains were the MJ&KC's. End 1909 = NOM&C takeover Dec 1, 1909. headway_min 480 = three trains each way (1903); an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide Jan 1904 p.923 (Sept 20, 1903), July 1907, Sept 1910; Greene County Herald 1914-01-09 p.1; Lemly ch. XXII (research report block [6]).

Traced with opstrace.py: 22.0 mi on the active CN Beaumont Subdivision, which OSM tags old_railway_operator='Bonhomie and Hattiesburg Southern Railroad', plus 4.1 mi of untagged rail into Hattiesburg. Fowler lists the GM&O Hattiesburg Branch (line 57, ex-MJ&KC) and the Bonhomie & Hattiesburg Southern (line 66) with identical stations and mileages (Beaumont 0 - Wingate 5.8 - New Augusta 7.6 - Mahned 10.4 - McCallum 18.9 - Hattiesburg 26.9), so this is taken to be the same track under a later owner; a separate OSM way tagged old_railway_operator=Mississippi Central (McCallum - Hattiesburg, abandoned) was not used. Waypoints Beaumont, Wingate, New Augusta, Mahned, McCallum all on the line; Hattiesburg 1.0 km off (town centre). No straight-line legs. LATER ALIGNMENT: today's corridor; the receivers practically rebuilt the branch in 1907-08 and from Feb 1, 1910 the NOM&C used the NO&NE Hattiesburg terminal - the Hattiesburg end is not verified for either era.

segments.note: Beaumont - Wingate - New Augusta - Mahned - McCallum - Hattiesburg: the original 1902 main line, a branch once Beaumont - Laurel opened Dec 20, 1903. Start 1903 is the first CONFIRMED year: the Dec 20, 1903 table (Jan 1904 Guide) runs through Mobile - Hattiesburg trains Nos. 4/1. Lemly says it opened for service Nov 17, 1902 (the Mississippi Rails history says Feb 1902 - SOURCE CONFLICT); no 1902 passenger evidence, so the 1902-1903 bracket is not drawn. March 1907: two trains each way. End 1909 = NOM&C takeover Dec 1, 1909 (continues on nomc-hattiesburg-branch). headway_min 720 = two trains each way (1907); an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide Jan 1904, July 1907 ('March, 1907'), Sept 1910 ('May 15, 1910'); Lemly ch. XXII; Fowler MS line 57 (research report block [7]).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 368.6 mi against a documented 366.5 mi (Sept 1910 Guide, Middleton - Mobile (Frascati); Fowler 368.6). Geometry reused from the successor GM&N layer (dataset PR #280, feature(s) gmn-mobile-union + gmn-union-middleton, whole), which was traced with opstrace.py over OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O, and cut here at station points geocoded with Nominatim and projected onto that line (uncut). MOBILE END: drawn to Frascati — the GM&N trace stopped about 0.6 mi short, south of downtown and NOT at the later Conception St. terminal, so a 0.6 mi OSM rail extension (opstrace.py, 5.2 mi of the extension trace on old_railway_operator=GM&O ways) carries it to today's TASD Frascati Yard; the exact 1897 Frascati station site is not verified. 1911 MOBILE TERMINAL NOT DRAWN: a new NOM&C passenger and freight terminal opened Dec 1, 1911 (Mississippi Rails corporate history), location not established (Lemly's 1909 plan: Augusta and Royal Sts, 1.2 mi north of Frascati); the 1911-1915 years are drawn to Frascati regardless. STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS inherited from the GM&N trace (3, 2.9 mi): south of Richton 1.5 mi, through Laurel 0.9 mi, near Sandersville 0.5 mi. Falkner - Middleton follows an untagged railway=abandoned way. LATER ALIGNMENT: the corridor as mapped today, which includes the 1910-11 Pontotoc relocation and the 1911 Decatur relocation (the 1909-1911 years draw the later line there).

segments.note: Mobile (Frascati) - Laurel - Newton - Union - Pontotoc - New Albany - Ripley - Middleton under the New Orleans, Mobile and Chicago ('PANAMA ROUTE'), which began operating the property Dec 1, 1909 after the MJ&KC foreclosure. May 15, 1910 table: Nos. 1, 5, 7, 11 / 2, 6, 8, 12. Frisco and L&N stock control from late 1911 and the receivership of W. F. Owen from Dec 19, 1913 did not change the operator. Evidence by year: 1910 timetable; 1911 Fowler 'Fay 1911G'; 1913 Coverdale report (detoured trains Feb-Mar 1913); 1913 or 1914 Cotton Plant wreck of the 'combination freight and passenger train' (Greene County Herald); Oct 1915 passenger train at the Little Creek flag station (Hattiesburg News, Mar 10, 1916). END IS [OPEN]: 1915 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service, NOT a known end. The NOM&C ran to Dec 31, 1916 and handed the Gulf, Mobile and Northern an operating railroad on Jan 1, 1917, so 1916 is near-certain, but nothing dated 1916 naming a passenger train was found. Do not extend to 1916 without evidence. 1917-1918 are undrawn on this layer and the GM&N layer alike (a known gap, not an assertion of no service). headway_min 480 is an estimate from the 1910 table (four train numbers each way, not all over the full line).
sources: Segment-level: research report blocks [1]-[6] and [13] — Official Guide Sept 1910 p.1001 ('May 15, 1910', Middleton - Mobile 366.5 mi); Fowler 'Fay 1911G'; Coverdale report 1913 quoted in Lemly ch. XXII; Greene County Herald 1914-01-09 p.1 (Cotton Plant mixed-train wreck, NOM&C); Hattiesburg News 1916-03-10 p.6 (passenger train at Little Creek flag station, Oct 1915).

Traced with opstrace.py: 22.0 mi on the active CN Beaumont Subdivision, which OSM tags old_railway_operator='Bonhomie and Hattiesburg Southern Railroad', plus 4.1 mi of untagged rail into Hattiesburg. Fowler lists the GM&O Hattiesburg Branch (line 57, ex-MJ&KC) and the Bonhomie & Hattiesburg Southern (line 66) with identical stations and mileages (Beaumont 0 - Wingate 5.8 - New Augusta 7.6 - Mahned 10.4 - McCallum 18.9 - Hattiesburg 26.9), so this is taken to be the same track under a later owner; a separate OSM way tagged old_railway_operator=Mississippi Central (McCallum - Hattiesburg, abandoned) was not used. Waypoints Beaumont, Wingate, New Augusta, Mahned, McCallum all on the line; Hattiesburg 1.0 km off (town centre). No straight-line legs. LATER ALIGNMENT: today's corridor; the receivers practically rebuilt the branch in 1907-08 and from Feb 1, 1910 the NOM&C used the NO&NE Hattiesburg terminal - the Hattiesburg end is not verified for either era.

segments.note: Beaumont - Hattiesburg under the NOM&C from Dec 1, 1909. May 15, 1910 table (Sept 1910 Guide): HATTIESBURG BRANCH Nos. 13, 15 / 14, 16, Hattiesburg 0 - Beaumont 26.9. From Feb 1, 1910 the NOM&C used the NO&NE's Hattiesburg terminal. END IS [OPEN]: 1910 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service, NOT a known end - no passenger evidence was found after the May 1910 table, and 1911-1916 is not established either way (Coverdale 1913 calls branch traffic 'negligible', which is not the same as no trains). Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 = two trains each way (1910); an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide Jan 1904, July 1907 ('March, 1907'), Sept 1910 ('May 15, 1910'); Lemly ch. XXII; Fowler MS line 57 (research report block [7]).

STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS (2, 2.6 mi): 0.4 mi from the main line at Lanham (Ellisville Junction) to the mapped grade's east end, and 2.2 mi from the grade's west end into Ellisville, where nothing is mapped (abandoned Dec 26, 1920). OpenHistoricalMap returned nothing here. The Ellisville terminal point is the town centre, not a verified station site.

segments.note: Ellisville Junction (Lanham) - Ellisville under the NOM&C from Dec 1, 1909. May 15, 1910 table: main-line trains 8/9 ran Laurel - Ellisville Junction - Ellisville (108.0) and back out to Ellisville Junction - Mobile, so the branch was served by main-line trains. END IS [OPEN]: 1910 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service, NOT a known end; 1911-1916 not established either way. The GM&N abandoned the branch effective Dec 26, 1920 - an abandonment, not a dated passenger end. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 1440 = one train each way; an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide July 1907 p.1022 ('ELLISVILLE BRANCH, March, 1907'); Sept 1910 p.1001; Lemly ch. V, XXII (research report block [8]).

The Pontotoc end draws the 1910-11 relocation.

segments.note: 3-ft gauge, steam. Gulf and Chicago Railroad (Falkner family; formed Feb 20, 1890 per Lemly, Aug 1, 1889 per msrailroads, from the foreclosed Ship Island, Ripley and Kentucky and the Gulf and Ship Island Northern Division). START IS [OPEN]: 1899 is the first CONFIRMED year - the Mar 1900 Guide prints a schedule dated February 1899 (two trains each way, one daily except Sunday and one Sunday only, about 3.5 h for 62 mi). The 1895 equipment roster (4 locomotives, 5 passenger cars) implies earlier service but is not a timetable, so 1890-1898 is not drawn. Do not move the start earlier without evidence. End 1903 = the MJ&KC took control July 1, 1903 and ran the line as its 'Gulf and Chicago Division' (feature mjkc-pontotoc-middleton). headway_min 1440 = one train each way on weekdays (1899); an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide Mar 1900 (schedule Feb 1899); msrailroads G&C page (1895 roster); Lemly ch. XXII (research report block [9]).

segments.note: Ripley Railroad, renamed Ship Island, Ripley and Kentucky (rename dated Mar 16, 1872 by Lemly, 1878 by msrailroads/Hoffman - SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved; one company either way). 3-ft gauge, steam from opening (the Memphis and Charleston advanced rails and rolling stock - Lemly), so Rule 5 trims nothing. Opening: Aug 30, 1872 per Lemly, 1874 per Hoffman (SOURCE CONFLICT). Drawn years are the CONFIRMED ones only: Fowler's line-55 entries name stations from the 1874 Official Guide (Tiplers, Luker's, Hopkins) and letter y (1875 Guide) on Ripley, Falkner and Middleton. END IS [OPEN]: 1875 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - the 1879 roster (2 locomotives, 3 passenger cars) suggests service continued, and the road ran until the 1889 foreclosure, but no timetable after 1875 was found. Do not extend without evidence. Ripley - Pontotoc (Gulf and Ship Island Northern Division, 1887-89) has no passenger evidence and is not drawn. headway_min is a placeholder estimate (no frequency sourced).
sources: Segment-level: Fowler MS line 55 (1874G station names; y = 1875 Guide); Lemly ch. XXII; msrailroads Ripley RR page (Hoffman); msrailroads G&SI Northern Division page (research report block [10]).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 24.4 mi against a documented 25 mi (Feb 1902 Guide statement; Lemly 'about 24'; Fowler 110.8 - 135.4 = 24.6). Geometry reused from the successor GM&N layer (dataset PR #280, feature(s) gmn-mobile-union), which was traced with opstrace.py over OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O, and cut here at station points geocoded with Nominatim and projected onto that line (Laurel 0.49 km, Bay Springs 0.04 km off the line). STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS inherited from the GM&N trace: part of a 0.9 mi leg through Laurel and 0.5 mi near Sandersville. LATER ALIGNMENT: the 3-ft K&CM was shut down at the end of 1902 and its roadbed 'reconstructed and standardized' into the MJ&KC main line (opened 1904); this draws that later standard-gauge main line as mapped today, not a verified K&CM alignment. The K&CM's Laurel terminal was at Kingston, 'just north of Laurel' (Lemly), not located.

segments.note: 3-ft gauge. Laurel (Kingston) - Welborn (later Hoy) - Mossville - Stringer - Bay Springs, 25 mi. [ANCHOR]: 1902 is the single proven year - the July 1902 Official Guide prints a company statement dated February 1902 that the road 'is operated for freight and passenger service'. Service certainly ran wider both ways (the K&CM bought the line Sept 1, 1901 and owned 2 passenger cars in 1901; the MJ&KC bought the roadbed June 30, 1902 and shut it down at the end of 1902), but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. The c.1899-1901 Kingston Lumber Co. logging-road years are excluded (Rule 1). headway_min is a placeholder estimate (no frequency sourced).
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide July 1902 (statement dated Feb 1902); msrailroads K&CM page (Hoffman); Fowler MS line 55; Lemly ch. XXII (research report block [11]).
